executive_summary: Project Meridian's core pricing engine is solid (12k req/s, P99 180ms), but go-live is at risk: every material threat sits in the external integrations and sign-offs, not the code. Two third-party vendors (Mapping vendor A, Payments provider B) have unresolved reliability bugs with fixes landing after our June 28 freeze, the Mapping vendor A SLA/MSA is still unsigned, a PCI security review is on the critical path but missing from the plan, and no incident owner is named for cross-vendor 3am outages. Recommend de-bundling the three cutovers and treating the July 15 date as at risk pending vendor commitments.

items.title: Mapping vendor A returning 5xx on ~3% of requests blocks the Surge 2.0 canary
items.owner: Lina (Backend Lead) / Mapping vendor A on-call
items.sla_or_rollback_note: No MSA/SLA signed, so vendor support is best-effort only. Pricing accuracy depends on ETA, so vendor instability directly gates the canary and there is no contractual remedy if it persists.
items.recommended_action: Get a written stability commitment and date from Mapping vendor A before scheduling the canary; set an internal error-rate threshold (<0.5%) as the gate.

items.title: Payments provider B refund webhook drops ~10% of callbacks; vendor fix lands after our freeze
items.sla_or_rollback_note: Vendor fix ETA 'end of June' falls after the June 28 go-live freeze, and reverting the PSP cutover is a config change (~20 min) needing a vendor-side cache flush, not a flag flip. Reconciliation double-counts in the meantime.
items.recommended_action: Build an idempotency/retry reconciliation shim on our side this sprint rather than depending on the vendor fix landing before freeze.

items.title: Mapping vendor A MSA/SLA (99.9% / P50<300ms) unsigned, so no production support tier
items.sla_or_rollback_note: Until the MSA is countersigned the vendor will not commit production support tiers or the 99.9% availability SLA. We would launch on a critical dependency with no contractual uptime or escalation path.
items.recommended_action: Escalate the MSA to legal as a go-live gate this week; do not schedule production cutover until countersigned.

items.title: No named incident owner for cross-vendor (Mapping vendor A / Payments provider B) outages
items.sla_or_rollback_note: The incident-ownership boundary is undefined across three organisations. At 3am it is unclear whether Northwind Rides, Mapping vendor A or Payments provider B leads triage, which will extend MTTR during a launch-window incident.
items.recommended_action: Define a cross-vendor incident RACI and escalation matrix; circulate before go-live sign-off and rehearse in a game-day.

items.title: PCI security review on critical path but missing from the plan
items.recommended_action: Add the 2-week PCI review (plus remediation buffer) to the critical path now and confirm the queue slot; treat any findings as a go-live gate.

items.title: Three cutovers (Surge, maps, PSP) bundled into one go-live window inflates blast radius
items.sla_or_rollback_note: Surge rolls back via feature flag in seconds, but maps and PSP are config cutovers (~20 min) needing a vendor-side cache flush. Bundling them means one failure forces a slow, multi-vendor rollback.
items.recommended_action: De-bundle the go-live: ship Surge 2.0 behind its flag first, then sequence the maps and PSP cutovers in separate windows with independent rollback runbooks.

items.title: Surge regression blocked on unfinalised Ramadan and public holiday multiplier table
items.recommended_action: Get Product to sign off the holiday multiplier table for both new markets this week to unblock the 14 failing regression cases.

items.title: App Store review and Arabic/French localisation lead times threaten the launch date
items.sla_or_rollback_note: iOS App Store review (3 to 5 days, external) stacks on top of a ~4-day localisation vendor turnaround: two serial external lead times that are easy to underestimate against July 15.
items.recommended_action: Pull localisation forward now and submit both apps to review immediately after; track the combined ~9-day lead time on the critical path.

items.title: Maps cutover breaks the A/B baseline used for the exec launch readout
items.recommended_action: Schedule the 2 to 3 day ETA baseline backfill before cutover so the launch readout keeps week-over-week comparability.

items.title: Payments provider B fee schedule unfinalised, so unit-economics modelling is incomplete
items.sla_or_rollback_note: Commercial terms with the PSP are unsettled, so unit economics for the launch business case cannot be locked.
items.recommended_action: Chase Payments provider B for the final fee schedule so Finance can close the unit-economics model before the steering decision.

top_3_actions_this_week: De-bundle the go-live and sequence the three cutovers: Surge (behind its flag) first, then maps and PSP in separate windows with independent rollback runbooks.
Escalate the Mapping vendor A MSA/SLA and a written stability commitment to legal and the vendor as a hard go-live gate.
Add the PCI security review to the critical path and ship the Payments provider B idempotency/reconciliation shim so neither vendor's slip blocks launch.
